description_en: Si Bāhāḥ is one of the majorbāhāhsof Patan. The main entry is to the west of the street, between rows of residential buildings and with an open space containing a Licchavi-eracaityain front. The carved door on the main western entrance is accentuated by two wall paintings and atoraṇaand is guarded by two stone lions. A two-storey building covered in traditionaljhingatītiles forms the front façade of the entrance and exhibits three small latticed windows on its first floor. A Buddhist statue is located on the left-hand side of the south wall of this entrance. The sunken courtyard measures 12.8 x 13.5 m (see site plan), and the main Bāhāḥ building is located on the west wing. The three-tiered temple can be seen in its entirety from its three-bay porch. Avṛttākāracaitya(205 cm high) is located at the centre of the courtyard, which is also home to twodharmadhātumaṇḍalas;one to the east (75 cm high) and the other to the west (80 cm high).The main temple is attached to the courtyard buildings to the south and is open to its back and to the north. A small (3 m wide) alley leads out to the street to the south. The four-storey temple faces east, and the main image of Buddha inbhaviṣyavyākaraṇamudrācan be visited through a single main door surmounted by atoraṇa. The entry floor has been secured with metal fences that reach up to the first floor. The plinth can be accessed by a flight of stairs and is flanked by two stone guardian lions and the national flag. A central five-foldpasukājhyāḥis located on the first floor of the principal east façade and is flanked by two small windows on either side. Small windows and blind windows painted in different colours can also be seen on the top floors. The floors are distinguished from one another with layers of painted cornices.All three of the Bāhāḥ's roofs are supported by beautiful carved and painted struts. Each of these three roofs has its own distinguishing features. The lowest roof is a single slanted lean-to-roof that slopes in towards the courtyard; the second roof is a traditionaljhingatīroof; and the top roof is clad in brass sheets. The upper and middle roofs are supported by struts displaying images of various gods, though the second floor also exhibits two corner struts displaying images of lizards, something that is rather unique tobāhāstruts. Threecaitya-shaped finials stand on the top of the building. The middle pinnacle is crowned with a parasol and flanked with bronze flags, whilst a metal banner hangs down from it. These pinnacles were donated by Dhana Thakuṃ and her three sons Dhanacā Muni, Rāja Muni and Harṣa Muni in 1850 (Śākya2535, 86). The courtyard has annex buildings on three sides, with the northern wing left free. Aphucācan be found on top of the southern roof. A five-bayphalcāis located on the ground floor, as well as a decorative carved entry door.This Bāhāḥ is not considered to be one of the 15 majorbāhās, however, it is on the list of the 18 majorbāhās. Alongside Co Bāhāḥ and Kipū Bāhāḥ, Si Bāhāḥ was added to the list of majorbāhasof Patan at a later date. Si Bāhāḥ is located two blocks in from the left side of the main street which runs from Naḥ Tola to Gāḥ Bāhāḥ. The Bāhāḥ can be accessed via a narrow street that leads to Pim Bāhāḥ (seeLAL0750). A woodentoraṇafixed above the entrance of the courtyard contains an image of Mahāvajradhara standing on top of lions in at its centre. Thistoraṇawas attached in 2012 after the previous one was lost. Entering through the door, one can see the chanting room on the right-hand side and stone images of Nāmasaṅgīti, Vasundharā and Āryatārā on the left. These images were established in 1982.A book preserved in the Bāhāḥcontains collections of chants and mentions that this building once only had two storeys. It seems, therefore, that the upper two storeys were added more recently (Śākya2535, 86). The sanctum of the Bāhāḥ is located on the ground floor of the building. The entrance of the sanctum is flanked by two metal images of Maudgalyāyana and Sāriputra. A small hole on the wall to the right of the entrance is worshipped as Hanumān. Above the entrance, one can find a bronzetoraṇawith images of Akṣobhya in the centre, Prajñāpāramitā to the right and Ṣaḍakṣarī Lokeśvara to the left. Inside the sanctum, a stone image of Buddha can be found standing in abhaviṣyavyākaraṇaposture. The original image of Buddha was made of wood, but it was replaced with this stone image in 1678 due to deterioration. Inside the courtyard, one can find twodharmadhātu maṇḍalasand acaitya. Mahākāla Cheli is located to the south and contains images of Mahākāla and other gods. Towards east of thecheli,meanwhile, one can find theāgamagharaof the Kvātha Bāhāḥ (LAL0660). Theāgamagharaof this Bāhāḥ lies to the east of the esoteric shrine, while residential buildings are located to the north.Inscriptions provide information about the initial construction of the monastic building. TheNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(19.3.26) mentions that Si Bāhāḥ was built after King Siddhinarasiṃha Malla (r. 1620-1661) passed rules regarding the fifteenvihārasof Patan. However, the information provided in the chronicle may be incorrect, since this Bāhāḥ is also mentioned in a colophon in thePañcarakṣāmanuscript copied in 1389 (NS 509) (Bendall1883, 191).
description_ne: ललितपुरका प्रमुख बाहा:मध्ये सि बाहा: पनि एक हो । ललितपुरका बाहा:हरूलाई १५ मूबाहा: र १८ मूबाहा: गरी दुई किसिमबाट गणना गर्ने परम्परा छ । ललितपुरका १५ मूबाहा:को गणनाभित्र सि बाहा: पर्दैन । पछि किपू बाहा:, चो बाहा: र सि बाहा: समेत समाहित गरी १८ मूबाहा: गणना गर्ने प्रचलन चलेपछि सि बाहा: पनि मूबाहा:भित्र परेको हो । यो बाहा: गा:बाहा:बाट पश्चिमपट्टि पुल्चोकतिर जाँदा सडकको उत्तरमा पर्दछ । बाहा:भित्र प्रवेश गर्ने मूलद्वारको माथि सिंहमाथि चढेका महावज्रधर अंकित काष्ठतोरण राखिएको छ । पुरानो तोरण हराएपछि नेसं ११३२ मा नयाँ तोरण राखिएको हो । मूल प्रवेशद्वारबाट भित्र छिरेपछि उत्तरमा भजन गर्ने कोठा बनाइएको छ । मूल प्रवेशद्वारको दक्षिणमा नामसंगीति, वसुन्धरा र आर्यताराका प्रस्तर मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । ती मूर्तिहरू नेसं ११०२ सालमा मात्र स्थापना गरिएका हुन् । बाहा: प्राङ्गणमा झर्ने सिँढीको दायाँ-बायाँ प्रस्तरको एक जोडी सिंह स्थापना गरिएको छ । बाहा: प्राङ्गणमा ढुंगा छापिएको छ । बाहा:को द्य:छेँ ३ तहको छानासहित चार तलाको बनाइएको छ । बाहा:मा रहेको भजन पुस्तकमा संग्रह गरिएको गीतअनुसार यो बाहा: पहिले दुई तलाको मात्र थियो, पछि जीर्णोद्धारको क्रममा चार तलाको बनाइएको हुनुपर्छ (Śākya 2535, 86) । द्य:छेँको सबैभन्दा माथिल्लो तेस्रो तहको छानामा पित्तलको पाता राखी गजुर स्वरूप तीनवटा चैत्य राखिएका छन् । बीचको चैत्यमा दायाँ-बायाँ झण्डा सहित छत्र ओढाइएको छ । नेसं ९७० मा धनककी पत्नी धन थकुं र उनका तीन छोराहरू धनचामुनि, राजमुनि र हर्षमुनिले राजा सुरेन्द्रविक्रम शाहको पालामा उक्त गजुर चढाएका थिए (Śākya 2535, 86) । पित्तलको उक्त छाना अड्याउन विभिन्न देवीदेवता अंकित टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । झिँगटीले छाइएको दोस्रो तहको छाना अड्याउन पनि विभिन्न देवीदेवता अंकित टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् तर ती टुँडालहरूमध्ये छेउका दुई टुँडालमा छेपारो राखिएका अंकित छन् । कुनै पनि बौद्ध विहारको टुँडालमा छेपारो अंकित भएको यो नै एकमात्र उदाहरण हुन सक्छ । बाहा:को पहिलो तलाको बीचमा पासुखा झ्याल राखी दायाँ-बायाँ एक-एकवटा साना झ्यालहरू राखिएका छन् । पहिलो तलाको माथि विभिन्न देवताहरू अंकित टुँडाल राखिएका छन् । भुइँतलामा बाहा:को गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ एक-एकवटा साना झ्यालहरू राखिएका छन् । ढोकामाथि पित्तलको तोरण राखिएको छ । तोरणको बीचमा अक्षोभ्य बुद्ध छन् भने दायाँ प्रज्ञापारमिता र बायाँ षडक्षरी लोकेश्वर छन् । ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ सारिपुत्र र मौद्गल्यायनको धातुमूर्ति पनि राखिएको छ । ढोकासम्म पुग्ने सिँढीको दायाँ-बायाँ एक जोडी सिंह, घण्टा र झण्डा राखिएका छन् । ढोकाको उत्तरमा एउटा प्वाल राखिएको छ । स्थानीयहरू यसलाई हनुमान् मानी पूजा गर्छन् । गर्भगृहभित्र भविष्यव्याकरण मुद्रामा रहेका बुद्धको प्रस्तर मूर्ति छ । पहिले यहाँ रहेको बुद्धको मूर्ति काठले बनेको थियो, काठको मूर्ति जीर्ण भएपछि नेसं 798 मा ढुंगाको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको थियो । बाहा: परिसरमा दुईवटा धर्मधातु मण्डल र एउटा चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । दक्षिणमा महाकाल छेलि रहेको छ जहाँ महाकालका साथै अन्य देवताहरू पनि स्थापना गरिएका छन् । महाकाल छेलिको पूर्वी छेउमा क्वाथ बाहा: (LAL0660) को आगमघर रहेको छ भने पश्चिम छेउमा दिगिभित्र जाने बाटो रहेको छ । बाहा:को पूर्वमा आगम रहेको छ । उत्तरमा आवासीय घरहरू रहेका छन् ।यो बाहा:को निर्माणसम्बन्धी जानकारी दिने कुनै अभिलेख भेटिएको छैन । नेपालिकभूपवंशावली (19.3.26) मा राजा सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लले ललितपुरमा रहेका विहारहरूको लागि नियम बनाइसकेपछि मात्र सि बाहा: निर्माण गरिएको कुरा उल्लेख छ । तर सिद्धिनरसिंह मल्लको शासनकालभन्दा धेरै अघि नेसं ५०९ देखि नै सि बाहा:को उल्लेख गरिएको प्रमाण भेटिएकोले (Bendall 1883, 190-191) सो वंशावलीमा दिइएको कुरा गलत भएको देखिन्छ । यस बाहा:को स्थापनाबारे स्थानीयहरू यस्तो पुराकथा सुनाउँछन्- नान्यदेवले सन् १०९७ मा सिम्रौनगढमा राज्य स्थापना गरेपछि त्यहाँ नयाँ दरबार बनाउन ललितपुरबाट कलाकारहरू झिकाएका थिए । ललितपुरका सुवर्णकीर्तिको नेतृत्वमा एउटा टोली सिम्रौनगढ पुग्यो । त्यहाँ दरवार बनाउन जग खन्दा एउटा बुद्ध मूर्ति भेट्टियो । उक्त मूर्तिलाई एक ठाउँमा राखेर दरबार बनाउने काम अघि बढ्यो । दरवार निर्माणको काम पूरा भएपछि सिम्रौनगढका राजाले खुसी हुँदै "के माग्छौ माग" भनेपछि कलाकारको नाइकेले दरबारको जग खन्दा भेटिएको बुद्धमूर्ति मागे । राजाले खुसी हुँदै उक्त मूर्ति उपहारस्वरूप दिए । मूर्ति साथमा लिएर ती कलाकारहरू ललितपुरमा फर्केपछि एउटा सभा गरे । सभाको निर्णयअनुसार ललितपुरको पश्चिममा रहेको एउटा पोखरीमाथि विहार स्थापना गरियो । त्यस पोखरीको पानीलाई नहर बनाई व्यवस्थित गरी न:टोलको ढुंगेधारा र छायबाहालको ढुंगेधारा गरी दुईवटा ढुंगेधारा बनाइयो । कलाकार टोलीको नाइकेको नामबाट विहारको नाम सुवर्णकीर्ति संस्कारित श्रीवच्छमहाविहार नामाकरण गरियो । कालान्तरमा 'श्रीवच्छ' शब्द अपभ्रंश भई सिबाहा: भन्न थालियो ।
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)

historical_events.event_description: 2012 CE: Kānchā Śākya and his wife Nānibeti Śākya donated a woodentoraṇawhich has been fixed above the outer entrance of thebāhāḥ.
Pañca donated a bell to thekvāḥpāḥdyaḥin 1882.

historical_events.event_name: The earliest mention of the bāhāḥ
historical_events.event_description: A colophon of thePañcarakṣāmanuscript copied in 1389 (NS 509) mentions thisbāhāḥ.This Nepalese manuscript has been preserved in the University Library of Cambridge.

Āsāmadu and his wife Bhikhvā Thakũ donated a gildedtoraṇacontaining images of Buddha, Prajñāpāramitā and Lokeśvara in the memory of their deceased parents Ratna Dhãju and Rānī Thakũ. This was fixed on top of the entrance of the sanctum where Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara lives.Daśakarmapratiṣṭhāwas also performed after the installation.
Śākyavaṃśa Joti and his family offered a copperdalūandmandaḥpāḥin 1662 CE.
Satya Nāyaka offered twophyagãs(wind bells) to Buddha in 1630.
Thakālī(leader) Yotiju, ten elderāḥjusand all of thesaṅghamembers of thebāhāḥenshrined a new stone image of Buddha in the sanctum in 1687 CE. The previous wooden image had deteriorated.
1595 CE: Led by Jīvarāja, Puhni Sevā Guṭhī donated a goldentoraṇaand fixed it above the entrance of the sanctum.
The members of the Vasuvāra Sevā Kharaka (Thursday Service Group) repaired the sanctum. They paved it inteliyātiles and changed two windows in the first floor in 1693 CE.

historical_events.event_name: The image of Buddha standing in the sanctum was covered with gilded plate
historical_events.event_description: 1630 CE: Budha, Bekha, Rūpasiṃha and others members of theguṭhīmade a donation for the Buddha image in the sanctum to be covered in gilded plate.

1700 CE:ThapāḥjuDharmasiṃha and the other ten elderāḥjusof thebāhāḥreplaced the previous regulations with new ones during the reign of King Yoganarendra Malla. According to the new regulations, the initiation ritual of a boy should not take place until he is 5 years old; the seniority system should not be avoided; drying clothes and other items at thebāhāḥplinths was no longer allowed; nails and thread were not allowed in thebāhāḥcourtyard; the bigger copper pot (jaḥsi) of thebāhāḥmay only be used forbāhāḥpurposes and cannot be rented out.Burleigh(1976, 47-48) has written a misleading translation of this inscription.
Dhāraṇī Saṅgha and members ofbāhāḥpaved the courtyard with stone in 1959 CE.
Punajoti, Dhãjoti, Candrajoti and others donated funds for the entrance door of the sanctum to be clad in brass plate in 1719 CE.

1824 CE: Dhanavantasiṃha Bhāro and his younger brother Rudranārā handed over the Dīpaṅkara image tothakālīDhaṃju, whose image was previously established in thebāhāḥ. Samyak bhojana(a feast) was arranged to commemorate this.
Lalitpur Sub-Metropolitan City and thesaṅgha-members of thebāhāḥrebuilt thedigichẽat the eastern side of thebāhāḥ.
